html:
SMTO-HTTP-0002 — The sign-in reply didn't include what SMTO needed

GUID: f3d2488d-e3b0-4b11-a439-08ea57bb77cd
Slug: http-auth-response-invalid
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO signed in to the service, but the reply was missing a value this connection expects, such as a session cookie or token, or wasn't in a usable form. Your main request wasn't sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store and select this HTTP Connection. Compare Session cookie, CSRF protection and any Extracted value rows under Advanced login settings with the service's sign-in documentation. SMTO looks for the sign-in value exactly where these settings point, so one wrong name means nothing is found.
  2. Correct any name or path that doesn't match the documentation, save, and select Test connection. The test signs in again and shows whether SMTO now finds the value.
  3. If the service uses OAuth, confirm in its documentation that it issues standard Bearer tokens. SMTO supports only Bearer tokens, so other token types fail at this step.

What success looks like

  • Test connection reports Reachable and Authenticated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the service's sign-in documentation, to the person who set up this HTTP Connection. Don't keep testing with unchanged settings; the reply will be rejected the same way each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • HTTP authentication extraction failed: a configured JSON Pointer, cookie or header value was missing, empty or oversized, a cookie contained control characters, the auth response exceeded 64 KiB or was incomplete, or an OAuth token response had a non-Bearer token type or invalid expires_in.

What this means

  • Authentication extraction returned a missing, oversized or invalid value, unsafe cookie, incomplete body, unsupported token type or invalid token/device response fields. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Authentication extraction returned a missing, oversized or invalid value, unsafe cookie, incomplete body, unsupported token type or invalid token/device response fields.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect sanitized response shape and configured extraction fields; never infer a wrong password from a parsing failure.

How to fix it

  • Compare the profile's login extraction rules (Session cookie, CSRF protection and Extracted value rows under Advanced login settings) or OAuth token endpoint against the API's documentation and the redacted auth_endpoint response preview in the request's activity. Correct the JSON Pointer, cookie or header names, then rerun Test connection. Only Bearer OAuth tokens are supported.
  • Inspect safe response shape diagnostics and correct extraction/session mapping using the API’s authoritative documentation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The documented response supplies valid required token, cookie and expiry fields within the authentication bound.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
